bounds: One session, one persisted credential identity, two completion candidates, two pollers, one cleanup transaction, clock0..3, session expiry1 and credential expiry3. Distinct identities never wrap or reuse.
fairness: Started operations settle under fair completion of KMS, database, delivery and cleanup transitions. The model permits request failures and lost replies. It does not require callers to initiate a request or cron to run repeatedly.
limitations: Policy admission and cryptography are abstract external authorities. The real PostgreSQL suite exercises the enrolled policy wrapper and test-only KMS.
Source request timestamps are captured before asynchronous transaction work. Expiry and the session-first cleanup lock are modeled explicitly; plaintext lost after consumption is not replayed.
Initial wrong-owner, missing-key and incomplete-cipher records cover reveal refusal. Arbitrary corrupted cross-session key references and automatic integrity repair remain outside this instance.
External revocation/owner/hash changes are sampled once while decryption is in flight. General API-key mutation and cache/inference authorization protocols require their own models.
One cleanup call is bounded here. Repeated cron sweeps, post-commit cache invalidation and revocation-service recovery remain outside this model.
Real conformance requires an isolated loopback PostgreSQL qa_* database; missing configuration is a failure, not a skipped proof.
